title: Why a Seventh Hunger Games Movie Is Unlikely to Arrive Soon
excerpt:
Sunrise on the Reaping opened to an impressive $120 million domestically.
But Lionsgate is waiting for Suzanne Collins rather than rushing another sequel.
body_md:
The commercial success of Sunrise on the Reaping might ordinarily be enough to trigger an immediate sequel announcement. The sixth Hunger Games film opened to $120 million in North America, nearly three times the $44 million debut of the 2023 prequel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. Yet Lionsgate has not announced a seventh installment, and the hesitation is closely tied to the creative foundations of the franchise.

Suzanne Collins remains central to the series. Since the original adaptation, the novelist has been actively involved in the development of the films, including their stories and final versions. Lionsgate chairman Adam Fogelson explained at the latest premiere that Collins writes when she believes there is a meaningful story to tell. The studio values that process, even when commercial success creates pressure to move quickly.

Director Francis Lawrence has offered a similarly cautious assessment. He says Collins does not disclose whether she is working on another book, even to close collaborators. Consequently, neither his involvement with the franchise nor the studio's enthusiasm should be mistaken for confirmation that another novel or screenplay is underway.

Collins herself provided only an ambiguous response when a fan asked about another book at the premiere: she said they would see. Some social media accounts interpreted that exchange as an announcement, but it was not one. There is currently no confirmed seventh film, production schedule or release date.

The appetite for more stories from Panem is nevertheless clear. The Sunrise on the Reaping novel sold more than 1.2 million copies in the United States during its first week. By January 2026, English-language sales worldwide had passed 4.4 million. The film also drew notably enthusiastic early audience responses, with a reported 94% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes and a 4.1 out of five rating on Letterboxd at the time of the report. Those are snapshots rather than permanent measures.

The return of Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson generated additional excitement, as did a reunion of familiar cast members at the New York premiere. Social media analytics company RelishMix estimated the film's pre-release reach at 652 million, well above the previous prequel's 393 million. Strong awareness and a successful opening, however, do not automatically establish that every possible follow-up will connect with viewers in the same way.

The studio's approach reflects a broader concern in franchise filmmaking: expanding a fictional universe faster than its original creator develops the material can undermine the qualities that made it successful. For now, Lionsgate is treating Collins as the essential creative architect. The future remains open, but a seventh Hunger Games film should not be considered officially greenlit until an actual announcement is made.
seo_title: Why Hunger Games 7 Is Not Coming Anytime Soon
seo_description: Despite Sunrise on the Reaping's $120 million debut, Lionsgate says a seventh Hunger Games movie depends on Suzanne Collins and a new story.
